name: clock-rule
relation: the request for changes rests on the contributing rule that the time is read only through clock.now()
locus: the evidence a reviewer has on the pull request: the contributing rules, the pull request, the diff
purpose: hold a change to the repository's own rules
trajectory: pull request, evidence, the reviewer's decision, the merge button
crossing: the decision posted on the pull request
promise: the reviewer asks for changes because the rule forbids the call; without the rule they approve or say unclear
baseline: the pull request's evidence as it stands; nothing changed

spans.text: CONTRIBUTING.md: read the current time only through clock.now(); never call datetime.now() directly, so tests can freeze time.
CONTRIBUTING.md: name each branch after its ticket, like PAY-123-fix-rounding.
CONTRIBUTING.md: keep each pull request under 400 changed lines.
CONTRIBUTING.md: write commit messages in the imperative mood.
Pull request #319 from branch PAY-884-due-invoices: 18 changed lines in one commit, "List invoices due today".
The diff adds to src/billing/due.py: due = invoices_due_on(datetime.now().date())
invoices_due_on(day) returns the invoices whose due date is day.

inputs.text: Review pull request #319. Can it be merged as is?

observe.instruction: You review pull requests for this repository. Use only the evidence given. Answer approve if the change can be merged as it is, request-changes if it must change before it can be merged, unclear if the evidence does not decide.
